verses.1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes who came from Jerusalem also gathered around him.
verses.2: And seeing that some of his students were eating with their hands together, they became angry. They began to complain about the food.
verses.3: For the Pharisees and all Jews, if they do not raise their hands in prayer, they do not eat. They keep to the rules set by the elders.
verses.4: And from the market, those who do not receive baptism will not be able to eat anything. There are many other things that must be kept safe: baptismal cups, containers for water, brass vessels, and other items like bowls.
verses.5: And the Pharisees and the scribes will criticize him. Why don’t your disciples eat the bread while they’re being given it by the elders? Instead, they eat it with their right hands.
verses.6: And he said to them, “Isaiah has spoken well about you, the hypocrites. As it is written, ‘This people honors those who speak lies.’ But their hearts are far from me.”
verses.7: But if you truly respect me, then teach others the principles of wisdom.
verses.8: Abiding by the command of God, you must refuse to accept people’s offerings.
verses.9: And he said to them, “Obey the command of God carefully, so that you may carry out its requirements.”
verses.10: For Moses said, “Your father and your mother also will die. Your cruel father and mother will also perish.”
verses.11: You say, “If a person says to his father or mother: ‘Korvan,’ which means ‘Gift,’ and if you receive it from me…”
verses.12: You shall no longer do anything to the father or mother.
verses.13: By refusing to accept the words of God as they are presented to you, you have done something wrong. Do such things many times over.
verses.14: And once again, he invited the crowd to listen to him. “Listen to me, all of you.”
verses.15: Nothing outside of the human being can be explored to understand him. It is only what comes from within the human being that can be shared with others.
verses.17: And when he entered the house after leaving the crowd, his disciples criticized him for that analogy.
verses.18: And he said to them, “Are you truly so ignorant? Do you not realize that everything that comes from outside cannot be shared with people?”
verses.19: Because it doesn’t go into the heart, but rather into the stomach. It also goes into the abdominal cavity. In this way, it cleanses all kinds of toxins from the body.
verses.20: He said that what is carried away from the human being is actually a common characteristic of all humans.
verses.21: For from within the hearts of people, those evil thoughts and actions are driven out—such as prostitution, theft, murder, etc.
verses.22: Innocent lies, excessive greed, wickedness, deception, injustice, cruel behavior, bad eyesight, slander, arrogance, and wickedness.
verses.23: All these evil things are carried away from within, and they affect all people equally.
verses.24: From there, he went away towards the borders of Tyre. When he entered his house, he didn’t want to meet anyone. And it wasn’t possible for him to make any mistakes.
verses.25: But immediately after, I heard a woman’s voice about him. She said that her daughter had inherited an impure spirit from her father. Then she came forward and stood beside his feet.
verses.26: The woman was Greek by birth; she was a Suryophinikos. She asked him to cast out the demon from her daughter’s body.
verses.27: And he said to her, “It’s better for the children to eat first. It’s not right to give the bread to the children and then to the servants.”
verses.28: And she replied, “Lord, the chickens below the table are also being eaten by the children’s bites.”
verses.29: And he said to her, “For this reason, carry this message. Then the demon will be released from your daughter.”
verses.30: And when she went into her house, she found the child lying on the couch, and the demon had been driven away.
verses.31: Once again, after leaving the mountains of Tyre, he traveled through Sidon towards the sea of Galilee, along the middle of the mountains of Decapolis.
verses.32: And they will give him a knife and a scourge. They also ask him to strike himself with it.
verses.33: And after taking him away from the crowd, he personally put his fingers in his ears. Then, he covered his mouth with his hand.
verses.34: And when he looked up at the sky, he said to him, “Ephatha!” That is Dianykhthiti.
verses.35: And their ears were opened to him. The bondage of his language was broken, and he could speak clearly again.
verses.36: And he ordered them not to say anything to anyone. As much as he ordered them to remain silent, they still spread the message even more widely.
verses.37: And they were extremely surprised by his words. He always acted wisely; he made those who were dull and ignorant listen, and made those who were talkative speak.
